name: The Robot Nobody Asked For

pick.label: Pick a job
pick.heading: Pick a job and hand it to a machine
lead: Everyone says AI and robots are coming for our jobs. So far they mostly write emails and vacuum the floor (badly). There must be better things for them to do.
Choose a job or a chore from the shelf, or your own, and invent the machine that takes it over. *Then decide what's left for the humans.*
pick.hint: Or click one to choose it.
pick.note: It doesn't have to work, and it definitely doesn't have to be legal. It just has to be something you'd secretly like to own. Total nonsense is welcome.

shelf.head: University
items: Finding a seat in the library

rows: Which job or chore are you handing over?
Boring, slow, stressful, embarrassing, or all four?
What is it, what does it look like, and how does it do the job?
Students, parents, companies, the city of Berlin?
What a human still has to do:
What can't the machine do, or what should it never be allowed to do?

values.hate: You refresh the website at 7 a.m. every day for three weeks, and when a slot finally appears it's in Spandau, on a Tuesday, at 7:15.
values.machine: A small robot on your desk that refreshes the website all night, grabs the first slot in Berlin and then rings a little bell. It's shaped like a tiger because it pounces.
values.who: Everybody who has ever moved flat in Berlin, which is everybody.
values.human: Actually going to the appointment, with all the right documents, in person. The robot tried once and was sent away for not having a passport.
values.name: “TerminTiger: It waits so you don't have to.”

yours.label: Your machine
yours.heading: Your idea
yours.lead: Fill it in on your own phone or laptop (it stays on your device), and be ready to tell the class about your machine in a few sentences.

rank.label: The ranking
rank.heading: Which machine wins?
rank.lead: Each student tells us about their machine in a few sentences. Add it, then argue it into place until everybody agrees.
